summary: Forest Service fire tower on Frosty Mountain, the high point of Amicalola Mountain; sources say it was removed and only footings remain.

facts.status_note: The Forest Service tower was removed; concrete footings remain in the old clearing.

access.note: The Approach Trail passes over the summit, on national forest land.

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. The Approach Trail goes over the summit.

events.note: USGS survey party found a fire tower on the summit and set a benchmark labelled FROSTY MTN FT.

notes_for_editor: Identity is inferred, not confirmed. The record's point (tnlandforms GA161 'amicalola mtn', 3,390 ft, Dawson) is the only Amicalola row; SummitPost and WillhiteWeb tie the former Forest Service tower to Frosty Mountain on Amicalola Mountain (WillhiteWeb gives 3,382 ft). No source checked gives Frosty's coordinates. Forest Lookouts lists Amicalola Mountain (Gilmer County, no status) and Frosty Mountain (Dawson County, Removed) as separate entries, so a human should decide whether they are one tower. The county conflicts: Dawson on tnlandforms, WillhiteWeb and the Frosty entry; Gilmer on the Amicalola Mountain entry and SummitPost's header. Status moved from unknown to removed on the strength of SummitPost and the Frosty entry. The name 'amicalola mtn' is the tnlandforms author's label (GA161, above 73). No build date, design, height or staffing appears in any source checked. Two WebSearch queries used.
